lines.trans: It hurts from here up to my neck, you know? I am all locked up.
You stay on the computer all the time, that is a problem. Cross your arms, take a deep breath, on three you tap, okay?
What is this, Fabrício?
It is my chiropractic side hustle. I only had this time slot. But tell me, did you stay in a hotel?
I am going to order my Uber, okay?
Oh, all right. Sorry about anything, it is a rush, you see? I really enjoyed it.
Someone already accepted, fast. Whoa, is it Fabrício?
Wait, it is Fabrício.
Wow, what a coincidence, right? Let's go because I left the car parked right out front.
Employee parking spot.

meanings.note: Used for taking transport, grabbing items, or taking an apartment first.

examples.trans: They will grab it ahead of me.
I do not need to take the subway.

meanings.note: Contraction of de + aqui.

examples.text: A dor pega daqui até o pescoço.
examples.trans: The pain goes from here up to my neck.
We are close to here.

meanings.note: In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.

examples.trans: See you later!
See you later. Thanks!

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: What is your job title?
Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Part of the body connecting head and shoulders.

examples.text: A dor pega daqui até o pescoço.
examples.trans: The pain goes from here up to my neck.
I have a pain in my neck.

meanings.note: Covers knowing facts or finding out information.

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.
Do you know the answer?

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number; before an adjective (todo travado) means completely.

examples.text: A culpa toda disso foi dele.
examples.trans: All the blame for this was his.
I am all locked up in my neck.

meanings.note: Used for sore, stiff muscles or a frozen computer.

examples.trans: My back is all locked up.
The screen froze.

meanings.note: Expresses staying in a place or state (ficar sentado, fica no celular).

examples.trans: You're going to stay seated.

examples.text: Ela fica no celular o dia todo.
examples.trans: She stays on her phone all day.

meanings.note: Limits a statement (eu só quero) or forms só que (except that / the catch is).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

examples.text: Só que agora ela precisa de ajuda.
examples.trans: Except now she needs help.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.

examples.trans: He is in the meeting.
She stays on her phone.

meanings.note: Desktop or laptop computer.

examples.trans: You stay on the computer all the time.
The computer froze again.

meanings.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun pointing to what was just said or done.

examples.trans: What is this, man?
That slows everyone else down.

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
It’s a marketing meeting.

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?
There are some good numbers.

meanings.note: Masculine noun despite ending in -a.

examples.text: Ficar só sentado é um problema.
examples.trans: Staying seated all the time is a problem.
Let's solve this problem now.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb (c -> ç before a/o).

examples.text: Abraça o corpo e respira fundo.
examples.trans: Cross your arms and breathe deeply.

examples.text: Ela abraçou as amigas na chegada.
examples.trans: She hugged her friends upon arrival.

meanings.note: Respirar fundo means to take a deep breath.

examples.text: Respira fundo e relaxa os ombros.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath and relax your shoulders.

examples.text: Preciso respirar um pouco de ar puro.
examples.trans: I need to breathe some fresh air.

meanings.note: Used adverbially in respirar fundo (to breathe deeply).

examples.text: Abraça o corpo e respira fundo.
examples.trans: Cross your arms and breathe deeply.

examples.text: Ele respirou fundo antes de falar.
examples.trans: He took a deep breath before speaking.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ela tá três anos aqui procurando.
examples.trans: She has been here for three years looking.
I have three things to sort out.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?
Are you in finance?

meanings.note: Here, to tap the table/shoulder as a signal during a stretch.

examples.trans: On three you tap, okay?
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.
What is this, man?

meanings.note: First-person singular possessive agreeing with the thing possessed.

examples.text: O seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?
That is my job.

meanings.note: Colloquial Brazilian term for temporary or secondary work beside a main job.

examples.trans: It is my chiropractic side hustle.

examples.text: Ele faz bico de garçom à noite.
examples.trans: He works a side gig as a waiter at night.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.

examples.trans: It’s a marketing meeting.
I’m in finance.

meanings.note: Manual spinal and joint adjustment therapy.

examples.trans: It is my chiropractic side hustle.
I had a chiropractic session.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
I’m not going.

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.
There are some good numbers.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: Appointed time or business hours.

examples.trans: I only had this time slot.

examples.text: Qual é o horário do voo?
examples.trans: What is the flight time?

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast. The informal thanks softens the refusal; it does not accept the invitation.

examples.trans: I’m not going, but thanks.
It’s a meeting, but I’m not going.

meanings.note: Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.

examples.trans: Hang on!
Who is there?

meanings.note: First-person singular object clitic.

examples.trans: Would you help me real quick?

examples.text: Por favor, me deixa morar aqui!
examples.trans: Please let me live here!

meanings.note: Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.
examples.trans: Let me tell you something.
They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Commercial lodging for travelers.

examples.trans: Did you stay in a hotel?

examples.text: O hotel fica perto da praia.
examples.trans: The hotel is near the beach.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: Used for ordering food or requesting an Uber.

examples.trans: I am going to order my ride now.
We already ordered dinner.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: Ah, ele veio fazer implante capilar?
examples.trans: Oh, he came to get a hair implant?
Oh, now I get it!

meanings.note: Neutral pronoun for 'everything / all of it'.

examples.trans: It was all inside him.

examples.text: Vai ficar tudo bem com ele.
examples.trans: Everything is going to be fine with him.

meanings.note: Modifies a verb to mean well or carefully, as in olhar bem (look closely).

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.
Everything is fine around here.

meanings.note: Used standalone in Brazilian speech as the everyday informal sorry.

examples.trans: Sorry, folks.
Sorry for the delay!

meanings.note: Indefinite determiner or pronoun; plural alguns means some or a few.

examples.trans: There are some numbers here.

examples.text: Alguns são bons, outros são ruins.
examples.trans: Some are good, others are bad.

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.
examples.trans: Let me tell you something.

meanings.note: Everyday Brazilian noun for a hectic pace or busy schedule.

examples.trans: Sorry about anything, it is a rush.

examples.text: A semana foi uma correria só.
examples.trans: The week was one big rush.

meanings.note: Gerund vendo pairs with estar (tá vendo, do you see), and tem que ver means we have to look into it.

examples.text: Você tá vendo aquela moça ali?
examples.trans: Do you see that young woman over there?
We need to look into that later.

meanings.note: Conditional eu gostaria softens a refusal (I would like to, but...).

examples.trans: I would like to, but I have work.
I really like this team.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.
I have many numbers here.

meanings.note: Doubled as já, já, it means 'very soon / any minute now'.

examples.trans: Your husband is already doing great.
I have already been in that situation.

meanings.note: Takes a direct object for payment methods or terms.

examples.trans: Do you all accept a deposit?
They do not accept delays.

meanings.note: Taking very little time; also used adverbially.

examples.trans: I will be right back, it is a quick thing.
The driver accepted quickly.

meanings.note: Friendly, upbeat Brazilian greeting or attention-getter.

examples.trans: Hey there, excuse me, my friend.
Hey there, it is me again.

meanings.note: Very common Brazilian exclamation expressing surprise, confusion, or pushback.

examples.trans: Huh, where is everyone?
Wait, aren't you going?

meanings.note: Very common mild Brazilian exclamation of surprise or amazement.

examples.trans: Wow, what a wild coincidence!
Gosh, it is already ten o'clock!

meanings.note: In forte aí, colloquial reaction to a wild coincidence.

examples.trans: Wow, that is wild, huh?
The coffee is very strong.

meanings.note: Conversational final tag seeking agreement or emphasis.

examples.trans: Cut that wire right now, okay?
Wow, that is wild, huh?

meanings.note: Points to a place away from the speaker; lá dentro reinforces inside there.

examples.trans: I'm going inside there.
Look in there.

meanings.note: Deixa eu + infinitive is the natural spoken Brazilian frame for let me...

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.
examples.trans: Let me tell you something.
Leave your phone on the desk.

meanings.note: Automobile; de carro means by car.

examples.text: A gente pegou o carro cedo.
examples.trans: We took the car early.

examples.text: Deixei o carro estacionado lá fora.
examples.trans: I left the car parked outside.

meanings.note: Left in a parking space.

examples.text: Deixei o carro estacionado aqui na frente.
examples.trans: I left the car parked right out front.
The motorcycle is parked over there.

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.
This here is a chart.

meanings.note: Used in na frente de (in front of someone).

examples.text: Não grita na frente dos outros!
examples.trans: Don't shout in front of everyone else!

examples.text: Te espero na frente da sala.
examples.trans: I'll wait for you in front of the room.

meanings.note: Here, a designated parking space.

examples.trans: I parked in the employee spot.
I did not find a parking spot on the street.

meanings.note: A worker employed by a business or institution.

examples.text: Esta é uma vaga de funcionário.
examples.trans: This is an employee parking spot.
The employee served the table.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).

examples.trans: All right, I'll go.
Some numbers are good.

meanings.note: Time between midday and evening; boa tarde! greets or bids farewell in the afternoon.

examples.trans: Good afternoon!

examples.text: A reunião é hoje à tarde.
examples.trans: The meeting is this afternoon.
